parameter_descriptions.params_json:
CONTRACT: one single-line JSON object (double quotes) with a top-level "scenario" (one of: convert_def_to_odb, report_wire_length, write_views). Object params such as pdk_binding / deck_vars are inline JSON objects, e.g. "pdk_binding":{"pdk":"nangate45","liberty":["/input/cells.lib"]}. Params named rtl/upf/sdc/text carry inline text; file paths go in *_file(s)/sources/netlist/def/gds keys as absolute /input/... paths. On failure read the envelope `error` field. Double-quoted JSON. Required: scenario, pdk_binding, exactly one of def_file/odb_file, tech_lef, cell_lef. Scenario-specific fields are documented by the agent README. Explicit params override pdk_binding.tool_policy.opendb_utilities and all decisions are recorded.
SCENARIO write_views WITH views=["powered_netlist"]: ALSO SUPPLY `cell_models` (or pdk_binding.cell_spice) -- the PDK cell netlist, e.g. sky130_fd_sc_hd.spice. IT IS REQUIRED FOR AN LVS-USABLE NETLIST. OpenROAD `write_verilog -include_pwr_gnd` emits only VPWR/VGND: it OMITS the bulk/well pins (sky130 VPB/VNB) and emits physical fill / decap / tap cells with an EMPTY connection list, because their power connectivity is implicit in the DEF rails rather than in its NETS section. Netgen then reports "Instance of <cell> has only 8 of 10 ports" and one port_match_error per instance, and LVS cannot match. With `cell_models` the tool reads each cell's DECLARED pin list from the PDK and connects every unconnected pin: power/bulk pins to their rails (override via pdk_binding.pg_pin_map for a node that names them differently), and every other pin to a UNIQUE per-instance net so a genuine open circuit STILL FAILS rather than being absorbed. MEASURED on a filled sky130 block: 258 vs 261 devices / 270 vs 267 nets / 1387 port errors WITHOUT it, versus 258==258 / 270==270 / 0 port errors WITH it. Omitting it does not error -- the envelope reports pin_completion.lvs_ready=false and the netlist will NOT match.
SCENARIO report_wire_length: optional `wire_length_source` (auto|detailed_route|global_route|hpwl, default auto) and `top_n` (default 10). The tool probes the database first and issues `report_wire_length -net * -detailed_route` when nets carry routed wires, else `-global_route` when a global route/guides exist, else (auto only) a per-net HPWL ESTIMATE that is recorded as a caveat and refused when instances are unplaced. An explicitly requested source that the database does not carry fails closed. Results carry total_wire_length_um, nets_reported and the top-N longest nets.
